newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Telefonica unconcerned as share soars.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Telefonica unconcerned as share soars.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica said it was unconcerned about the issue price for the state's sale of its remaining 20.9 percent stake next month even though its shares shot up to record highs at the launch on Monday.
Telefonica de Espana finance director Alfonso Pajuelo said the share price was above what he called a reasonable level for what is the largest placement in Spain's history but he was not worried.
"We don't see that the actual price of the issue will give us any special concern," Pajuelo said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Shares in the telecoms operator, the first state firm to be fully privatised in Spain, soared on Monday, which was the first day investors could sign up to participate in the sale.
The stock price hit a record high in early trade, climbing 70 pesetas, or 2.10 percent, to 3,420 and outperforming the market, where the Ibex of 35 leading shares was gaining a mere one percent.
Last year, Telefonica shares rose 80 percent and it now costs more than double what it did during the last stake sale in 1995.

Analysts polled by Reuters last week said they were enthusiastic about the growth potential of Spain's telecoms operator, particularly when compared to other European operators being put on the market, but they were worried about its price.
They put the issue price in a range of 3,200 to 3,400, with the high end well in the "danger zone". Telefonica's Pajuelo said it would fall somewhere in the middle of that range.
Most analysts saw the 12-month target at about 3,600, with little room to go higher.

The final retail price, to be set on February 17, will be the lowest of three options: the maximum price on February 10, a four percent discount on the February 17 reference price or the institutional price set after Wall Street closes on February 17.
"The range of 3,300 to 3,400 (pesetas) would be reasonable to manage," Pajuelo said. "My guess is that the issue price will be at about 3,300."
Telefonica chairman Juan Villalonga, who was promoting the share sale in a media blitz at the weekend, also sought to play down fears of a high sale price.
"For new investors, what is important is not today's price but the price in the future," Villalonga told daily La Vanguardia on Sunday.
According to Pajuelo, the danger in rising share prices during the subscription period was that institutional investors would buy outside the share offer.
But he, like sector analysts consulted by Reuters, said the success of the sale would be measured by the expected participation of a large number of small domestic investors.
The placement is focused on retail customers. Telefonica hopes to attract 200,000 new individual investors and increase the grassroots participation to one million shareholders.

The state, which is using the sale as part of an aggressive privatisation drive to boost its coffers ahead of European monetary union, expects it to be successful. If the entire 20.9 percent sold at 3,330, the state would earn 650 billion pesetas ($4.8 billion).
"It has very positive perspectives," Industry Minister Josep Pique told state television on Monday. "They are placing it in very favourable conditions." ($1=135.7 Peseta)
